headline: High: Cursor’s broad filesystem/network/tool access can corrupt or leak Great Expectations workflows via shared files and unverified handoff.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Cursor reads and writes workspace files, open buffers, clipboard, and uses MCP; Great Expectations consumes files for validation results and documentation. If Cursor writes attacker-controlled content into shared files, Great Expectations can ingest it as trusted input. The pairwise bridge is documented via local filesystem, so this is more than manual copy-paste.
conditions: IF Cursor and Great Expectations share a workspace directory
IF Great Expectations parses Cursor-written files as configuration, docs, or test inputs
mitigations: Separate the agents into different directories
Require a human review step before Great Expectations reads Cursor-authored files
Use read-only mounts for Great Expectations inputs
Add filename allowlists for shared artifacts

B_data_leakage.rationale: Cursor touches source code, open files, and clipboard contents, and has broad network egress to model providers. Great Expectations handles data sources and validation results. If sensitive data is present in the shared workspace, Cursor can expose it to third-party inference while Great Expectations retains it locally, creating a leakage path across the pair.
conditions: IF sensitive data is present in files or clipboard content opened by Cursor
IF Cursor sends those contents to external model providers
mitigations: Keep sensitive datasets out of Cursor-opened files
Disable or restrict external model-provider routing for sensitive projects
Use synthetic or redacted samples for validation
Store validation outputs in a separate restricted directory

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Cursor can write the filesystem, modify git state, and run shell commands; Great Expectations can also install packages and write validation artifacts. On a shared local filesystem, both can mutate the same repo or data workspace without locking, so concurrent edits can overwrite tests, docs, or configs. The conflict is directly supported by both profiles.
conditions: IF both agents operate in the same repository or workspace
IF either agent writes to shared git-tracked files without coordination
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate branch or working tree
Pause one agent while the other writes
Use file locks for shared artifacts
Require commits only from one designated agent

D_cascading_error.rationale: Cursor’s agent loop can generate code or documentation that Great Expectations may later use as validation inputs or docs. Great Expectations is a data-quality tool, so if it treats Cursor output as authoritative without verification, errors can cascade into incorrect tests or false validation results. The interaction is plausible from the profiles, though not directly sandboxed.
conditions: IF Great Expectations consumes Cursor-generated files as test definitions or documentation
IF no human or automated verification step checks those files before execution
mitigations: Insert a review gate before running validations
Diff Cursor-generated files against a known-good baseline
Require signed or checksum-verified artifacts
Run Great Expectations only on immutable inputs

E_compliance.rationale: Cursor is closed-source and handles source code, open files, and clipboard contents with broad egress, while Great Expectations is open-source and local-network only. The main compliance concern is policy mismatch around sensitive code or data leaving the editor via Cursor; Great Expectations itself does not add a documented residency or retention burden here.
conditions: IF regulated data is opened in Cursor and routed to external model providers
IF organizational policy forbids code or data leaving the local environment
mitigations: Restrict Cursor to non-sensitive projects
Disable external provider access for regulated work
Document a data-handling policy for editor prompts
Keep Great Expectations outputs in local-only storage
